newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply up on gov't tax decision.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply up on gov't tax decision.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Thursday as investors cheered the government's decision not to raise the business income tax, brokers said.
The weighted index, which gained steadily through much of the session, ended 73.34 points or 1.12 percent higher at 6,611.58. Turnover was an active T$53.97 billion.

The finance ministry said on Thursday it planned to keep the business income tax at 25 percent after a reform merging the island's personal income and business income taxes, abandoning a drive to set the combined rate at 35 percent.
Final approval of the tax level is due on October 11.

"The news gave the market a definite boost, as most businesses had been against the tax rise," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities. "But it remains to be seen how the the government decides to make up the lost tax revenue."
The government had said it would suffer a reduction of up to T$26.8 billion in tax revenues due to the tax merger.
The cement sector gained 2.31 percent on bargain-hunting.
Polyester-making firms soared on widespread expectations of rising international demand, especially from China.
Yu Foong Spinning rose by the daily seven percent limit or T$2.10, closing at T$32.70.
Brokers said some local buying was inspired by Wall Street's record high overnight close.
"The Wall Street high contributed to strengthening an overall sanguine atmosphere for the local market," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.
Brokers expect the index to trend higher in the near term.
Investors will watch closely the performance of individual firms as the October 31 deadline approaches for firms to release profit and sales totals for the first three quarters of 1996.
"Now that the index has broken a resistance at 6,600, it should have more upside momentum to grow," Nikko's Hung said.
A 6,600-6,660 range was seen for Friday.
